title: Developer Time Is Valuable - Use the Right Tools - Kilian Valkhof

developers. I&#39;m here joined today by
Kellyan Valkov. Um and we know each
other for decades from conferences and
stuff and then we haven&#39;t talked for
years right?
&gt;&gt; So, how are you doing?

probably like the early frontiers
conferences that we first first met,
right? That&#39;s a long long time ago.

have not heard of Frontiers conferences,

were very much web focused and web
standards focused conferences in
Amsterdam all the time. At the same
time, we had Par web which was kind of
similar as well. And before that we had
app media in London. Like these were all
the the heydays of these like web
development days where we talked about
how about using standards which brings

article which was also in the newsletter

nowadays a lot of them not being APIs
that are browser or web standards APIs
anymore but actually dependent on the
company. What do you what do you mean by

&gt;&gt; Yeah, so uh it like the the reason I

I built my own browser Poly Pane. We we
can talk about that later. uh but that

that looks just like any other bit of
JavaScript API. So you have like
document getelement by ID and you have
navigator.jolocation.
So it it looks like any any API
um but it&#39;s not available in my browser
by default and it is in Chrome, in
Firefox, in Safari etc. So I was getting
questions about that. Uh and then every
time I explained people why and this is
to like developers that have been
building websites for like 5, 10, 20
years as well. uh they were very
surprised
uh not necessarily because of what I
told them but because they hadn&#39;t
themselves like thought through that. So
what the geoloccation API does is
ideally it asks the operating system
give me the user&#39;s physical location and
the operating system runs on hardware
with a GPS tracker in it or a GPS
receiver and it can query GPS and get uh
a value back. But of course not all
devices have a GPS receiver built in.
Um, so what the browser then does is it
just sends your IP to Google&#39;s
geoloccation service and asks the Google
geoloccation service
where is this IP located and then the
service does whatever it does and it
sends back the uh geoloccation to the
browser.
In other words, you&#39;re sending user data
to Google uh or to Apple
um or or to Microsoft and uh and then
getting results back. Uh but of course
because it feels like just any other
JavaScript API
uh there&#39;s you know people didn&#39;t
realize that that was what was
happening. And the reason it doesn&#39;t
work in my browser in polyane is because
of course Google gets to use Google
services for absolutely nothing in
Google Chrome. Like they have the the
super secret unlimited usage key built
into Google Chrome. But every other
browser
essentially needs to pay Google to use
that service um because it&#39;s a service
they offer and they like to make money
apparently. Um, and so to use it in my
browser, I ask people to add their own
Google API key to make those API calls.
And so this surprised a lot of people,
but there&#39;s actually quite a lot of APIs
in browsers that feel like they just
exist, like you know, interacting with
the DOM or uh doing console.logging
blogging or whatever, but that are
actually like calling out to these
services that these same very large
